question: A leucoma is a dense white corneal opacity through which the iris details cannot be seen, distinguishing it from a nebula (faint haze through which iris is visible) and a macula (moderate opacity, iris details partially visible).

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This is TRUE. Leucoma = dense white opacity, iris details invisible. Compare: Nebula = faint haze (iris clearly visible); Macula = iris partially visible. The grading is clinically important for surgery planning.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. The standard grading: Nebula (faint, iris fully visible), Macula (moderate, iris partially visible), Leucoma (dense white, iris NOT visible), Adherent leucoma (with iris incarceration). This grading determines surgical eligibility.
